# T2.03: the faulting address

Neither serial.log nor the unified log reports MMU faults (the driver doesn't log them). RM does report them per
channel: `NV906F_CTRL_CMD_GET_MMU_FAULT_INFO` (0x906f0106) on the channel object returns the address, type and a
string, and clears them. It works on GSP-RM through our client.

Added:
- `chan_fault()` in `src/channel.c` (that control).
- In `encode1`, when the error notifier is set: the fault info and a map of every buffer (GPU range, sys/vid), with the
  faulting one marked.

Result, 256x128 QP 26:

```
MMU fault info -> 0x0: address 0x20000c000 type 2 "FAULT_PTE"
  input      0x0200000000..0x020000c000 sys
  ...
```

`FAULT_PTE` (no mapping) at exactly the end of the input picture: luma 256x128 = 0x8000 plus chroma 256x64 = 0x4000
(block-linear, block height 2 GOBs). The engine reads past the input surface. The next 16 KB (up to `recon` at
0x200010000) is unmapped VA. Next (T2.04): find out why. Candidates: chroma read with luma height, a different unit
or base for `chroma_top_frm_offset`, a larger block height than we tile with, or read-ahead past the frame.
